newsitem.title: USA: U.S corp bond new issue activity off to slow start.
newsitem.headline: U.S corp bond new issue activity off to slow start.

text.p: A typical slow start to the week should not last for long as a positive market tone is expected to draw out any potential issuers still on the sidelines, dealers said.
"It's a typical slow start to the week," said one syndicate source. "There's still not much talk of new deals going on but at these levels issuance should pick up."
High-grade syndicate sources said with U.S. Treasury yields at lower levels, issuers contemplating tapping the market may be prompted to move up their debt financing.
"The market still has a good tone to it and I think we'll continue to see new issues come without any forewarning as has recently been the case," said another syndicate source.
Despite the absence of a calendar for straight corporate debt issues, preferred deals continue to dominate with a number of issues waiting in the wings, dealers said.
"Preferreds should continue to dominate the calendar for the next few weeks," said one high-grade syndicate source. "Out of about 20 deals that I know of about 18 are preferred issues."
ITT Harftord is expected to bring about $20 million in preferred shares to market via Goldman Sachs & Co, sources said.

Meanwhile, among other issues expected are ABN Amro with a $500 million five-year subordinated note deal via ABN and Morgan Stanley. Price talk on the issue is 40 to 43 basis points over Treasuries, syndicate sources said.
Nationale Bank de Paris is also expected to tap the market with about $500 million in debt in early November, sources added.
Goodyear is still expected to issue $100 million in 10-year debt via Goldman Sachs & Co, dealers said.
International Home Foods Inc is expected to price $400 million in senior 144A notes due 2006 via Chase Securities, sources said.
Unifrax is expected to price $100 million in seven-year senior notes later this week.
Coca-Cola FEMSA is expected to issue $175 million in 10-year notes via JP Morgan Securities.
Chase Telecommunications is also expected to price $105 million in senior discount notes, dealers added.
In the government market, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was up 5/32 at 99-17/32 to yield 6.79 percent.
